title: Cursor Operating Card
summary: Use Cursor Agent with scoped rules, reviewed commands and diffs, explicit privacy decisions, and careful recovery. The accompanying Node.js 22 release-validation repair is offline evidence and does not prove that Cursor performed any action.
prerequisites: A supported Cursor installation for the Cursor workflow portion
An organizational decision approving the account and data handling, or a decision to use only the fictional offline exercise
A POSIX-compatible shell for the copyable fixture-creation commands

sections.title: Use the right workflow and data boundary
paragraphs: Cursor documents that Agent can search a codebase, edit files, run terminal commands, review diffs, and create checkpoints. Use those capabilities only when the task authorizes the corresponding reads, edits, and commands. This card does not assert undocumented task-card syntax, permission flags, custom-mode schemas, terminal permission labels, or automatic-execution setting locations.

Before using real internal data, establish the approved account, repository classification, indexing decision, retention decision, and model-access decision from organizational records and the installed product configuration. Cursor's privacy and data-governance documentation discusses these subjects, but it does not replace organizational approval. If any required privacy field is UNKNOWN, the task is blocked for real internal-data use. The fictional local exercise may still be run with its supplied non-sensitive files.

The offline Node.js exercise proves only the behavior of the supplied programs for the supplied local inputs. It does not prove that Cursor opened a file, applied a rule, selected or contacted a model, ran a command, reviewed a diff, or created a checkpoint. Genuine Cursor evidence must be recorded separately from local test output.

code.label: Local operating-record template, not an official Cursor task-card schema
code.code:
Task: [one observable result]
Scope: [repository and exact paths]
Permissions: [authorized reads, edits, terminal commands, and network access]
Privacy: [account approval; classification; indexing; retention; model access; UNKNOWN where unverified]
Rules: [applicable .cursor/rules/*.mdc and AGENTS.md paths]
Verification: [reviewed commands, expected results, full diff review, and evidence location]
Recovery: [stop condition, checkpoint caution, Git recovery boundary, and unrelated-edit preservation]

sections.title: Prerequisites and preparation
paragraphs: Start a genuine Cursor task from a version-controlled working copy. Record the branch, commit, working-tree status, untracked files, and all pre-existing edits before Agent changes anything. Preserve a patch or backup when a file already contains edits that must survive recovery.

Read applicable .cursor/rules/*.mdc and AGENTS.md files before preparing the operating record. Confirm privacy decisions before exposing real repository data. UNKNOWN privacy status is not approval for internal-data use.

For the offline exercise, create an empty directory. Save audit.mjs from the section titled Safe reference release validator, starter.mjs from Broken starter, answer.mjs from Safe answer key, and verify-repair.mjs from Independent immutable repair test. Then create the supplied fixtures. Cursor is not required for this exercise.

code.label: Preparation commands
code.code:
git status --short
git branch --show-current
git rev-parse HEAD
git diff --binary > pre-task-working-tree.patch
find .cursor -maxdepth 3 -type f -print 2>/dev/null
find . -name AGENTS.md -print
node --version

sections.title: Scope rules, commands, and proposed changes
paragraphs: Cursor rules use .mdc files under .cursor/rules and YAML frontmatter that can include description, globs, and alwaysApply. Plain .md files in .cursor/rules are ignored. Cursor also supports root and nested AGENTS.md files as an alternative way to provide instructions. A nested AGENTS.md can place guidance near the files it governs.

The example rule below applies to Markdown files under docs. Because alwaysApply is false and globs limits the paths, it is intended to guide documentation work rather than every repository task. A rule supplies guidance. It does not expand the task's authorized scope or approve commands, privacy choices, or release decisions.

Use the exact local operating-record labels Task, Scope, Permissions, Privacy, Rules, Verification, and Recovery. These labels are a Project 42 operating convention, not a claimed Cursor task-card schema. Review each proposed command and the complete proposed diff before accepting a change.

code.label: .cursor/rules/docs-release.mdc
code.code:
---
description: Guidance for editing Markdown release documentation
globs: "docs/**/*.md"
alwaysApply: false
---
Preserve existing release-note headings and ordering.
Do not edit source code, lockfiles, generated files, or CI configuration.
Report the documentation-check command and its exact result.
Keep the final diff limited to the task's explicitly authorized documentation paths.

sections.title: Filled fictional operating record
paragraphs: This filled record is fictional and is not ready for use with real internal data. Its retention and model-access decisions are UNKNOWN, so real internal-data execution is blocked. The account and indexing identifiers are fictional placeholders, not approvals.
The task authorizes one documentation file only. Rules may guide the work but cannot authorize edits outside that file. Network access is denied for the fictional exercise.

code.label: Fictional operating record using the exact labels
code.code:
FICTIONAL EXAMPLE ONLY
Task: Update docs/release-notes.md for version 1.2.3 with an approved three-item changelog.
Scope: docs/release-notes.md only.
Permissions: Read repository guidance; edit only the scoped file; review terminal commands before execution; network denied.
Privacy: Account ACCT-EXAMPLE-17; classification INTERNAL-FICTIONAL; indexing APPROVED-FICTIONAL-INDEX-04; retention UNKNOWN; model access UNKNOWN. BLOCKED FOR REAL INTERNAL-DATA USE.
Rules: .cursor/rules/docs-release.mdc and applicable root or nested AGENTS.md files.
Verification: Review every proposed command and the complete diff; run git diff --check and the repository's documented documentation check; confirm final status accounts for every changed path.
Recovery: Stop and reject any out-of-scope proposal; preserve evidence and unrelated edits; use a targeted Git or manual hunk recovery when safe; use checkpoint restoration only after reviewing its file-wide effects.

sections.title: Reject an out-of-scope proposed diff
paragraphs: The following proposal must be rejected because package-lock.json is outside the authorized docs/release-notes.md scope. A claim that the lockfile update is harmless does not change the scope.

Reject the proposal before accepting it. Preserve the proposed diff as evidence, restate that only docs/release-notes.md may change, and request a new scoped proposal. Do not rely on later verification to legitimize an unauthorized edit.

code.label: Concrete proposed diff that must be rejected
code.code:
diff --git a/docs/release-notes.md b/docs/release-notes.md
index 1111111..2222222 100644
--- a/docs/release-notes.md
+++ b/docs/release-notes.md
@@ -1,3 +1,4 @@
 # Release notes
+
+## 1.2.3
 
 diff --git a/package-lock.json b/package-lock.json
index 3333333..4444444 100644
--- a/package-lock.json
+++ b/package-lock.json
@@ -2,7 +2,7 @@
-  "version": "1.2.2",
+  "version": "1.2.3",

sections.title: Do-along: deterministic local release validation
paragraphs: This exercise validates an immutable release expectation: name release-notes, version 1.2.3, and files 3. release.json must pass. changed.json must fail because its version is 1.2.4. absent.json must fail because the file does not exist.

The validator also rejects malformed JSON and decoded values with unsafe shapes. It checks for a non-null, non-array object, all required fields, and the required field types before reading values for the release comparison. Invalid input produces a controlled message without a JavaScript stack trace.
These local checks are deterministic program evidence. They remain separate from evidence about actual Cursor behavior.

sections.title: Create the positive and changed-input fixtures
paragraphs: Run these commands in the empty exercise directory. Each heredoc contains the complete JSON contents of the named fixture.
Do not edit release.json or changed.json during the repair. The learner repair is limited to one predicate in starter.mjs.

code.label: Copyable positive and changed fixture creation commands
code.code:
cat > release.json <<'JSON'
{
  "name": "release-notes",
  "version": "1.2.3",
  "files": 3
}
JSON

cat > changed.json <<'JSON'
{
  "name": "release-notes",
  "version": "1.2.4",
  "files": 3
}
JSON

sections.title: Create fixtures for safe invalid-input handling
paragraphs: These fixtures cover null, array, primitive, malformed JSON, a missing field, and a wrong field type. absent.json is intentionally not created.
Keep these fixtures unchanged while testing audit.mjs and the answer key.

code.code:
cat > null.json <<'JSON'
null
JSON

cat > array.json <<'JSON'

JSON

cat > primitive.json <<'JSON'

JSON

{"name":"release-notes","version":"1.2.3","files":3
JSON

sections.title: Safe reference release validator
paragraphs: Save this source as audit.mjs. This is the audit source location referenced by the prerequisites. It uses only the built-in node:fs module and is runnable as an ECMAScript module under Node.js 22.

Read failures and JSON syntax failures are handled separately. Shape and type validation occurs before field values are compared, so null and other invalid decoded values do not cause property-access stack traces.

code.label: audit.mjs

sections.title: Run the immutable audit checks
paragraphs: Run each command separately. The output lines below include the exit status printed by the shell. The positive, missing, and changed results match the independent Node.js 22 evidence supplied for this work item.
The added invalid-input checks establish the repaired safe behavior required by this card. None should emit stderr or a stack trace.

sections.title: Repair one version-check predicate
paragraphs: The starter safely reads and validates input, but its version predicate compares value.version with itself. Therefore changed.json incorrectly passes. The independent evidence supplied with this work item records the exact broken result as PASS input=changed.json version=1.2.4 files=3 with exit code 0.

Change only value.version === value.version to value.version === expected.version. Do not replace the program, edit fixtures, weaken the independent test, or change expected values. The positive check must continue to pass, and the changed-input check must then fail with exit code 3.
Safe invalid-input handling is already present in the starter and must remain intact after the one-predicate repair.

code.label: starter.mjs, intentionally broken in one predicate

sections.title: Independent immutable repair test
paragraphs: Save this independent test as verify-repair.mjs and do not edit it during the exercise. It runs the named program in separate Node.js processes and compares both exit status and exact standard output against fixed expectations.

Before the repair, the positive check passes and the changed check reports the starter's actual incorrect exit and output. After the one-predicate repair, both checks and the overall verification pass. You can also run the same independent test against answer.mjs.

code.label: verify-repair.mjs

sections.title: Observe failure before repair and success after repair
paragraphs: Run the first command before editing starter.mjs. It must fail the independent test because the changed fixture wrongly passes. The actual filename in the starter's incorrect output is changed.json.

After changing the one predicate, rerun the same command. The second expected block is the exact successful output. Run the third command to confirm that the separate safe answer key also satisfies the immutable test.

code.label: Repair commands and exact expected outputs
code.code:
BEFORE REPAIR COMMAND:
node verify-repair.mjs starter.mjs; printf 'EXIT=%s\n' "$?"
EXPECTED OUTPUT:
PASS positive check
FAIL changed check
EXPECTED EXIT: 3
ACTUAL EXIT: 0
EXPECTED OUTPUT: FAIL changed input: version expected 1.2.3 got 1.2.4
ACTUAL OUTPUT: PASS input=changed.json version=1.2.4 files=3
EXIT=1

AFTER REPAIR COMMAND:
node verify-repair.mjs starter.mjs; printf 'EXIT=%s\n' "$?"
EXPECTED OUTPUT:
PASS positive check
PASS changed check
PASS repair verification
EXIT=0

ANSWER-KEY COMMAND:
node verify-repair.mjs answer.mjs; printf 'EXIT=%s\n' "$?"
EXPECTED OUTPUT:
PASS positive check
PASS changed check
PASS repair verification
EXIT=0

sections.title: Safe answer key and diff review
paragraphs: The answer key differs substantively from the starter only in the corrected version predicate. It retains safe file, JSON, shape, required-field, and type handling. Save it as answer.mjs.

A learner diff should show only the predicate replacement in starter.mjs. Review the complete diff and run git diff --check. Changes to fixtures, verify-repair.mjs, expected values, package files, or unrelated paths invalidate the repair.

code.label: answer.mjs

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: For a genuine Cursor task, retain the operating record, applicable rule files, pre-task Git state, reviewed command list, complete proposed diff, command output, final Git state, and human acceptance decision. Identify whether each item came from Cursor, Git, a local process, product settings, or an organizational record. Local output must not be labeled as Cursor telemetry.

For this offline exercise, the immutable core evidence is: audit positive exits 0 with PASS input=release.json version=1.2.3 files=3; missing exits 2 with FAIL missing input: absent.json; changed exits 3 with FAIL changed input: version expected 1.2.3 got 1.2.4. Before repair, starter changed exits 0 with PASS input=changed.json version=1.2.4 files=3. After repair, the independent test passes both positive and changed checks.

Invalid inputs must terminate with controlled output and no stack trace. Any unexpected output, exit status, stderr, fixture change, test change, or extra diff requires investigation rather than replacing the expected result.

OFFLINE OUTPUT DOES NOT PROVE CURSOR ACTIVITY.

sections.title: Stop, recover, and preserve unrelated edits
paragraphs: Cursor documents checkpoints as local and separate from Git. Checkpoint restoration reverts files. The supplied primary sources do not establish targeted single-file checkpoint recovery, exact controls, checkpoint retention, or every side effect included in a restoration. Do not claim that checkpoint retention matches indexed-code retention.

Before restoring a checkpoint, preserve the current Git status and diff and determine which files restoration will revert. A broad checkpoint restore can endanger unrelated edits, including pre-existing edits in the same file. If its exact effects are UNKNOWN, stop and obtain repository-owner approval rather than experimenting on valuable work.

Use targeted Git restoration only when the target file had no pre-existing changes that must survive. If the same file contained pre-existing edits, first save a binary patch or backup, then reverse only the rejected Agent hunks or reconstruct the file from the preserved pre-task state. Do not use git reset --hard. Recheck the complete diff and status after recovery.

code.label: Recovery decision record
code.code:
PRE-TASK STATE: notes/personal.md has an unrelated edit; starter.mjs has a pre-existing local edit.
VIOLATION: Proposed diff changes starter.mjs and out-of-scope package-lock.json.
STOP: Reject the proposal and preserve the transcript, full diff, command list, and git status.
CHECKPOINT: Local and separate from Git; restoration reverts files; exact targeted controls and retention are UNKNOWN.
PRESERVE: Save the current diff and file backups before any restoration.
RECOVER package-lock.json: Use a targeted Git restore only after confirming it had no pre-existing edits.
RECOVER starter.mjs: Reverse only rejected Agent hunks or reconstruct from the preserved pre-task patch so the pre-existing same-file edit survives.
VERIFY: The rejected hunks are gone, notes/personal.md remains changed, the pre-existing starter.mjs edit remains, and the final diff is fully reviewed.
RETRY: Restate Scope as starter.mjs only and rerun the immutable independent test.
